PR title: fix(supervisor): guard the supervisor socket path against Unix domain socket length limits (#5845)

PR description:
## What

Closes #5845. The controller and wake sockets both already fall back to a sha256-hashed `/tmp` path when their canonical `.gc/*.sock` path would exceed the ~104-108 byte Unix domain socket path limit (macOS/Linux respectively) — the supervisor socket had no equivalent guard, so a long `GC_HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` fails the bind with an opaque `bind: invalid argument` instead of falling back like its two siblings.

## Fix

A one-to-one copy of the existing `controllerSocketPathLimit`/`wakeSocketPathLimit` pattern: `supervisorSocketPathLimit = 100`, falling back to `/tmp/gascity-supervisor/<sha256(dir)[:16]>.sock` when the canonical path exceeds it. The existing `guardSupervisorSocketDir(dir)` call is unchanged.

New tests (`cmd_supervisor_test.go`): short dir unchanged (regression guard), long dir falls back correctly, fallback is deterministic per-dir, and two different long dirs don't collide (needed since `supervisorSocketPathCandidates()` feeds both a live and default path).

## Follow-up fix included in this PR

While validating this change against the full local test suite, two pre-existing tests — `TestRunSupervisorWarnsOnEphemeralAPIPort` and `TestRunSupervisorNoWarningForLowAPIPort` — started hanging indefinitely. Root cause: both tests force `runSupervisor` to fail its control-socket bind fast (a deliberate synchronous fast-exit trick, since neither test otherwise cancels `runSupervisor`'s context) by pre-occupying the canonical `RuntimeDir()/supervisor.sock` path with a directory. Since `t.TempDir()`-based `GC_HOME` routinely produces a canonical path over the new 100-byte limit, the new fallback silently redirected the control socket to a different (short, unoccupied) `/tmp` path — bypassing the tests' directory collision, so the bind succeeded and `runSupervisor` ran forever in its reconcile loop instead of returning.

Fixed by computing `sockPath` in both tests via `supervisorSocketPath()` (the same resolution `runSupervisor` itself uses) instead of hardcoding the canonical path, so the tests' directory-collision setup lands wherever the code will actually bind, fallback or not. Confirmed both tests now pass in <0.1s; confirmed they hang without this fix; confirmed they pass in <0.1s on stock `main` (which never had a fallback to bypass).

## Validation

- `go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...` clean, `gofmt -l .` empty
- `go test -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/gc/... -run 'TestSupervisorSocket|TestReloadSupervisorFallsBack|TestRunSupervisorWarnsOnEphemeralAPIPort|TestRunSupervisorNoWarningForLowAPIPort'` all pass
- Full local push-gate run: the `cmd/gc` shard containing the affected tests passes clean; remaining failures across other shards and `unit-core` are pre-existing environmental/timing flakes (dolt-compaction timeouts, lsof-based probes, detached-probe/systemctl-timeout tests, process-signal-timing tests) unrelated to this change, confirmed via direct package/test lookup
- Pre-commit lint clean (0 issues) on both co [truncated]

Linked issue #5845: supervisor: socket path has no length guard, unlike the controller and wake sockets — a long GC_HOME/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR dies with "bind: invalid argument"
## Symptom

`gc start` prints `gc: supervisor did not become ready; see <supervisor.log>`. The log ends with

```
gc supervisor: listening on supervisor socket: listen unix /…/gc/supervisor.sock: bind: invalid argument
```

Nothing says why. The path is over the platform's `sun_path` limit (104 bytes on macOS, 108 on Linux), which `bind(2)` reports as `EINVAL`.

## Root cause

`supervisorSocketPathForDir` (`cmd/gc/cmd_supervisor.go:249-251`) is a bare `filepath.Join(dir, "supervisor.sock")`, and the `net.Listen` at `:626` wraps the error without mentioning the limit. `dir` comes from `supervisor.RuntimeDir()` (`internal/supervisor/config.go:266`): `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/gc`, else `GC_HOME`, else `~/.gc` — so an operator-set `GC_HOME` or `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` of about 90 bytes is enough.

The other two unix sockets already guard this: `controllerSocketPathLimit = 100` (`cmd/gc/controller.go:76`, applied at `:115-119`, sha256 fallback under `/tmp/gascity-controller/`) and `wakeSocketPathLimit = 100` (`internal/nudgequeue/state.go:19`, applied at `:174-183`; its comment cites the 108/104 limits). The supervisor socket is the one that never got the treatment.

## Reproduction

I verified the failure directly on macOS 15: `net.Listen("unix", p)` for a 155-byte `p` returns exactly `listen unix …/supervisor.sock: bind: invalid argument`. I have not run `gc start` under a 90-byte `GC_HOME`; nothing between `RuntimeDir()` and the bind looks at the length, so that is the gc-level trigger:

```
GC_HOME=/tmp/$(printf 'x%.0s' {1..90}) gc start
```

## Environment

upstream `main` at c374d5247 (2026-09-01), macOS 15 / Darwin 25.6; the Linux limit is 108.

## Fix candidates

1. Add `supervisorSocketPathLimit = 100` and reuse the siblings' sha256-fallback shape in `supervisorSocketPathForDir`, relocating an over-long path to `/tmp/gascity-supervisor/<hash>.sock`. About ten lines plus a test; the three sockets then behave the same. Preferred.
2. Check the length before `net.Listen` at `:626` and fail with an error that names the limit and the env var that produced the path. Smaller, but the operator still has to move the directory and the sockets stay inconsistent.

## Adjacent / out of scope

#3452 (closed as a duplicate of #2312) and #2312 are the test-side flakes of the same limit; neither adds a runtime guard. #5770 is a different path-resolution problem (herdr's `os.UserConfigDir`).

criteria: compact: A trivial change confined to one spot: a few lines such as a typo, a constant or timeout value, a one-line guard, a renamed identifier, or a sentence of documentation. It needs at most one small test adjustment. Adding a helper, restructuring a code path, or adding several regression cases is not compact.

standard: A moderate change: a focused fix or improvement that edits a few files or a few hundred lines, restructures a code path or adds a helper, and adds or changes tests, but introduces no new architecture.
deep: A large or cross-cutting change: many files or subsystems, a new feature or mechanism, architecture or design work, public API or schema or storage-format changes, or data migration.
